newsitem.title: USA: NRC official fined for leaking investigation.
newsitem.headline: NRC official fined for leaking investigation.

text.p: A former Nuclear Regulatory Commission official on Friday was ordered to pay a $5,000 fine for giving a Maine nuclear plant confidential information from a criminal investigation.

U.S. District Magistrate David Cohen declined to order jail time for Edouard Trottier, who was the NRC's project manager for the Maine Yankee plant, saying Trottier had suffered enough by losing his career over the incident.

Trottier, 54, pleaded guilty in March to leaking to Maine Yankee four pages from an investigation into whether plant officials fraudulently manipulated a safety test used to justify a power increase in the late 1980s.
U.S. Attorney Jay McCloskey said the investigation - launched by an anonymous whistleblower's letter in late 1995 - was still ongoing. Plant officials have denied wrongdoing in the safety testing.

According to court documents, Trottier said he sent the documents because he wanted to "level the playing field" between the plant and the media. He told reporters Friday he mistakenly thought the document had already been made public.
"It was not a mistake to be excused ... but it was a mistake of the head not of the heart," Trottier's lawyer Peter DeTroy told the court. Trottier could have received six months in prison.
Prosecutors had urged jail time, arguing Trottier's action allowed Maine Yankee to learn the names of employees who were secretly cooperating with the NRC and Department of Justice investigators.

"(Because of Trottier's action) whistleblowers may conclude that it is better to be silent about safety violations than to risk losing their jobs," Assistant U.S. Attorney Donald Clark told the court.

Maine Yankee has had a series of equipment problems over the past three years. Efforts to restart the 25-year-old plant in Wiscasset were suspended last month while its owners seach for a buyer or decide to shut it down permanently.
Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, and 22 percent by other New England utilities.
